title: Add password visibility toggle to lock screen
head: 849b050cc3c2
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new reveal control is mouse-only on a keyboard-operated lock screen
leads.consequence: A user without a usable pointer cannot toggle visibility to inspect a typed password. No keyboard or accessible press action changes passwordVisible, despite the password field already handling keys. Add a keyboard or accessible action and test it.
leads.triage: verified in source (eye is MouseArea-only); pre-existing design of the original commit, unchanged by follow-up; dropped as out of follow-up scope

leads.summary: Clicking reveal on an empty field arms plain text for the next password
leads.consequence: With no password entered, click the always-enabled eye and start typing: echoMode is already TextInput.Normal, so newly typed password characters appear unmasked until a later clear/blank/re-toggle. Clearing a previous attempt and clicking the icon produces the same state. If a reveal is intended only for already-entered text, guard empty input and add an empty-field test.
leads.triage: verified in source; reveal on empty field is an explicit user choice, not a defect; dropped

leads.summary: The copy/cut structural tripwire never runs on headless test runs
leads.consequence: If no compositor is reachable, require_compositor exits successfully before the source-only Copy/Cut assertions. This is precisely a check that does not need Quickshell or Wayland, so removing either key guard remains undetected in headless CI. Run the structural check before the compositor gate, leaving the QML fixture gated.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N2); corroborated; published

leads.summary: Open face-auth PR #8336 conflicts with both the changed reserve property and fingerprint fixture
leads.consequence: Both changes modify the same input margins and the same fingerprint fixture. PR #8336 replaces fingerprintReserve with iconReserve and its fixture reads iconReserve; this PR adds rightIconsReserve = fingerprintReserve + visibilityToggleReserve and its fixture reads rightIconsReserve. Keeping either version's fixture/reserve unchanged in a combined version leaves the other fixture reading an absent property; retaining the face PR's input margins alone drops the new eye reserve, and retaining only this PR's reserve leaves the face-only input without a face allowance. The integration needs an explicit combined reserve and updated fixture assertions if both PRs merge.
leads.triage: confirmed by coordinator gh api (#8336 open, dirty, touches same reserve lines and fingerprint fixture) and Opus draft check; published as related-PR note

leads.summary: Open PR #7680 independently adds a second reveal button and incompatible visibility state
leads.consequence: Both PRs add the same eye glyph pair and separate state properties to the same password field. If their new controls survive a merged version without consolidation, users get two eye buttons whose state can diverge; resolving the echoMode conflict by keeping one state means the other control no longer reveals the text. Choose a single implementation or reconcile the states and fixtures before merging both.
leads.triage: confirmed by coordinator gh api (#7680 open, clean, same field reveal toggle) and Opus draft check; published as related-PR note

limits: Source-level boundary hunt only, no Quickshell UI or Qt native process executed, and no user input injected. H1/H2 are directly determined by this QML's event and property bindings, not a claim about Qt clipboard internals.
Open-PR merge consequences H4/H5 depend on a future human conflict resolution. The overlapping definitions and fixtures are confirmed, not an assertion that GitHub automatically merges broken code.

PKGBUILDs reside in a different repository according to docs/file-layout.md:8-31. The only added runtime file is within the already-shipped shell tree; the new tests/fixtures stay repo-only and are discovered by the glob in test/shell:10-13.

flags.claim: fails when any single fix except the copy/cut guard is reverted
flags.why: Reverting (removing) the copy/cut guard does fail the test: the rg check reports 'LockView.qml no longer has: StandardKey.Copy with an accept StandardKey.Cut with an accept' and the test exits 1. What the test misses is the guard kept but made ineffective (Keys.priority: Keys.AfterItem), which is not a revert.
flags.fix: ... passes on this head, and fails when any single fix is reverted, including removal of the copy/cut guard. It does not catch a guard that is kept but no longer runs first (details below).
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: test fails on every single-fix revert including guard removal; misses only a kept-but-ineffective guard

flags.claim: host the view in a Window, run with QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ..., put a sentinel in Quickshell.clipboardText, and call keyClick(Qt.Key_C, Qt.ControlModifier, -1). That separates a working guard from both a removed one and one that runs after the field.
flags.why: Dropped parts of the recipe that make it meaningful. Ctrl+C only copies a selection in Normal echo mode (qquicktextinput.cpp 3297-3303), so without revealing the field and selecting the text first the keypress copies nothing even with a broken guard, and the test passes vacuously. My probe also focused the field in an active window (requestActivate, then waited for win.active && input.activeFocus) before sending keys; keyClick is a method of a TestEvent instance.
flags.fix: ... host the view in a Window, run with QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ..., reveal the field, give it focus and select its text (for example selectAll() or Ctrl+A), put a sentinel in Quickshell.clipboardText, and call keyClick(Qt.Key_C, Qt.ControlModifier, -1) on a TestEvent. ...
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: TestEvent recipe now reveals, focuses and selects before keyClick

flags.claim: a password revealed and left unsubmitted within 5 s of suspend would still be revealed after resume, until the next idle blank
flags.why: Lost a condition. Quickshell deletes the lock surface of a screen that goes away and creates a new one for a new screen, which creates a fresh LockView with passwordVisible false. The reveal only survives a resume that keeps the same outputs; Service.qml 36-39 says such resumes happen, so the path is plausible, but it is not unconditional. My own final.md H1 had the same omission. It is also measured from the last input (the idle timer is re-armed by every key and pointer move), not from the reveal.
flags.fix: ... a password revealed and left unsubmitted, with suspend starting within 5 s of the last input, would still be revealed after a resume that keeps the same outputs, until the next idle blank.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: suspend note conditioned on 5 s from last input and a resume that keeps the same outputs

flags.claim: from the 100th failure at that size, the attempt count is cut again
flags.why: The overshoot covers counts 100 to 999 only. At size 18 without a sensor, 'Authentication failed (1000)' is drawn at 15 px and is not truncated.
flags.fix: from the 100th to the 999th failure at that size, the attempt count is cut again
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: impact limited to 100th to 999th failure

flags.claim: Counts up to 999 behave the same way.
flags.why: Missing lower bound. Counts 1 to 99 fit at that size; only three-digit counts (100 to 999) overshoot.
flags.fix: Counts from 100 to 999 behave the same way.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: counts from 100 to 999

flags.claim: Small corrections to the reply: with a fingerprint, floor-limited elision starts at six digits at size 20 (seven at 19).
flags.why: The numbers are right in my environment, but the reply did not say six digits fit. It said counts up to four digits hold and 'a seven digit count at base 19 and 20 reaches the elide backstop', both of which my sweep confirms. This is a refinement, not a correction. My final.md section 2.2 had the same framing. It is also font- and rendering-dependent.
flags.fix: Drop it, or phrase it as a precision note: 'at size 20 six digits already reach the floor'.

flags.claim: Idle blanking is global rather than per monitor; every screen's view still re-masks.
flags.why: The idle timer and runBlank() are global, but the per-screen displaysBlank value can differ from the shared flag while a video wallpaper is shown, because it follows Hyprland's per-monitor DPMS state. So 'rather than per monitor' is too absolute, and the reply's 'drives displaysBlank per screen' is partly true. The second half is right: runBlank() clears monitorDpmsKnown, so every screen's binding goes true and every view re-masks (source, not run).
flags.fix: The idle blank is triggered for all screens at once; screens only differ through Hyprland's DPMS state while a video wallpaper is shown. Every screen's view still re-masks.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: blanking triggered for all screens at once, screens differ only via Hyprland DPMS with a video wallpaper

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13183#issuecomment-5839046929) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13183#issuecomment-5846876181), checked on `849b050c`.

**Outcome:** all four earlier findings are resolved on this head. Each fix was exercised in headless runs of the lock view; the primary-selection path and the lock service's blank/wake wiring rest partly on source (see Test scope). Two small new points follow: an edge case in the new status-line fit, and a copy/cut test that does not catch an ineffective guard.

| Earlier finding | Status | What was checked on `849b050c` |
|---|---|---|
| Revealed password reaches the clipboard and primary selection | Resolved | With the field revealed, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Shift+Del, Ctrl+Insert, the Copy/Cut keys, and Ctrl+A or Shift+Home followed by Ctrl+C no longer change the clipboard. On `27bb736a` each of them copied the password. Mouse drag, Shift+click and double-click select nothing, and a click clears a keyboard selection before the release that would copy it to the primary selection. |
| Failure message truncated, attempt count hidden | Resolved | With a fingerprint enrolled, counts up to four digits stay visible at every `omarchy display text size` from 9 to 20. |
| Reveal stays on through idle blanking | Resolved | Blanking re-masks, waking does not re-reveal, and the typed text is kept. |
| Input-method hint parity (optional) | Resolved | The effective hints are the same in masked and revealed mode. |

**Verified:** the earlier verified behavior still holds: the toggle moves nothing at any text size from 9 to 20, with or without a fingerprint, and the overflow and fingerprint fixtures pass. The new `lock-password-visibility-test.sh` is picked up by `test/shell`, passes on this head, and fails when any single fix is reverted, including removal of the copy/cut guard. It does not catch a guard that is kept but no longer runs first (details below). A long revealed password now shrinks to fit the field.

### Status-line fit can still overshoot by a fraction of a pixel

`statusTextScale` scales the full-size measurement linearly against the full line width. Glyph advances do not scale exactly linearly, so the chosen size can land just past the line. At display text size 18 without a fingerprint, `Authentication failed (100)` is sized to 16 px, needs 259.03 px of a 259 px line, and renders as `Authentication failed (10…`. Counts from 100 to 999 behave the same way.

**Impact:** from the 100th to the 999th failure at that size, the attempt count is cut again, which is the case the fix set out to remove. The new test checks only the fingerprint case, so it does not catch this.

**Suggested change:** keep a small margin, as `passwordDotScale` and `plainTextScale` already do:

```qml
Math.min(1, (statusTextNode.width - 4) / statusMetrics.advanceWidth)
```

With that change the case above renders at 15 px and fits, and the PR's fixture still passes.

### Optional test improvement: copy/cut test does not catch an ineffective guard

This concerns test coverage only; the guard works on this head. The `rg` check confirms that the guard text exists, not that it runs. With the guard kept but `Keys.priority: Keys.AfterItem` added (the dependency the reply identifies), Ctrl+C and the other copy/cut keys copy the revealed password again, and `lock-password-visibility-test.sh` still passes. The check also sits after `require_compositor`, so it is skipped wherever the file is skipped, although it needs no compositor.

**Impact:** a later change that breaks the guard without deleting its text leaves the clipboard exposure open with a green test.

**Suggested change:** drive real key presses. `TestEvent` from `QtTest` ships with qt6-declarative (a Quickshell dependency) and works under Quickshell without `qmltestrunner`: host the view in a `Window`, run with `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` so nothing appears on the desktop, put a sentinel in `Quickshell.clipboardText`, reveal the field, give it focus and select its text (for example with `selectAll()` or Ctrl+A), then call `keyClick(Qt.Key_C, Qt.ControlModifier, -1)` on a `TestEvent`. Without the reveal and selection, Ctrl+C copies nothing even with a broken guard. That separates a working guard from both a removed one and one that runs after the field. At minimum, moving the `rg` check above `require_compositor` lets it run on headless machines.

### Notes on the reply

- **Hard timer for the reveal:** the blank-based re-mask covers the reported case. One related path was traced from source only and not run: if suspend starts within 5 s of the last input, a revealed, unsubmitted password would still be revealed after a resume that keeps the same outputs, until the next idle blank. A Qt `Timer` would not bound that either, because timers do not advance during suspend.
- **Polkit:** in `PolkitAgent.qml`, `responseVisible` follows PAM's echo flag for the prompt, so plain text appears only for prompts PAM marks as visible. It is not a user-controlled password reveal, so the reasoning here does not carry over directly.
- **Per-monitor blanking:** the idle blank is triggered for all screens at once; screens only differ through Hyprland's DPMS state while a video wallpaper is shown. Every screen's view still re-masks.

**Related open PRs:** #7680 adds its own reveal toggle to the same password field, and #8336 changes the same fingerprint reserve and fixture. Both touch `LockView.qml` in overlapping lines.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of `shell/plugins/lock/`, the new and changed tests, and Qt 6.11.2 and Quickshell 0.3.1 sources. Headless Quickshell runs (offscreen platform, default monospace font) loaded the production `LockView.qml` from `849b050c` and `27bb736a`, drove real key and mouse events through a window, swept text sizes 9 to 20 with and without a fingerprint, and ran the lock fixtures and the new test against single-fix reverts. No live Wayland compositor or desktop session was used. The primary selection is not available offscreen, so that path rests on source plus the observed empty selection at release. X11-only key bindings, Service blank/wake wiring and the suspend path come from source, not observation.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
